item.description:
Hamas commander Samir Abu Younis killed in Israeli strike on Khan Younis

Hamas' armed wing said on Sunday that a senior commander who helped plan and oversee the 7 October 2023 attack on Israel had been killed in an Israeli airstrike.

The Al-Qassam Brigades identified the commander as Samir Abu Younis, 53, the commander of its Rafah brigade, and said he was killed on Saturday.

The Israeli military said on Sunday it had struck a senior commander in Hamas' armed wing but did not identify him.

Medics said Abu Younis was killed and others were wounded in an airstrike that targeted him in a street in the Mawasi area of Khan Younis in the southern Gaza Strip.

Hamas said Abu Younis joined Hamas' armed wing in 1991 and had held several senior operational roles in Rafah before becoming commander of the brigade.

Hamas said his funeral would be held on Sunday afternoon in Khan Younis.

An October ​2025 ceasefire halted major fighting but has not stopped Israeli attacks or secured Hamas' disarmament.

Gaza health authorities say at least 1,600 Palestinians have been killed since the ceasefire went into effect. Five Israeli soldiers have been killed ​during the same period.

Palestinian authorities say more than 74,000 people have been killed in Israel's military campaign against Gaza, launched after Hamas-led fighters killed about 1,200 people in southern Israel in October 2023.

Report by AFP

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] Eisenkot calls Netanyahu's unity government call 'yet another spin move'
item.description:
Eisenkot calls Netanyahu's unity government call 'yet another spin move'

Israeli opposition leader and prime ministerial hopeful Gadi Eisenkot has accused Benjamin Netanyahu of resorting to political tricks to delay the formation of a new government, saying his latest call for negotiations was "yet another spin move".

In a post on X, Eisenkot said Netanyahu knew that a meeting between the negotiating teams of Likud and Yesh Atid had already been scheduled for Monday.

"This is the latest bluff: Netanyahu calls for negotiations after they have already been scheduled, claims he wants unity, but disgraces a state ceremony in the Knesset and divides and incites as if there were no tomorrow," Eisenkot wrote.

The remarks come after an inconclusive election left the Knesset without a clear governing majority, with rival political camps seeking to assemble the numbers needed to form the next government.

Eisenkot said Netanyahu knew he had lost the election and that there was "an overwhelming majority against him among the citizens of Israel and in the Knesset".

He accused the outgoing prime minister of mounting "a delaying action" to make it difficult to form a new government and prevent the replacement of the Knesset speaker.

Eisenkot reiterated that the conditions for joining an emergency government under his leadership included acceptance of the principles he had outlined and "a break with the extremists".

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] Trump may not attack Iran as long as it doesn't provoke US, report says
item.description:
Trump may not attack Iran as long as it doesn't provoke US, report says

President Donald Trump has told senior advisers in recent days that he may hold off on attacking Iran if the US faces no new provocations from Tehran or the Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen, according to three people familiar with the matter.

Trump has alternated between threats of escalating the war with new strikes and winding down hostilities, and current and former officials say he does not appear to have made up his mind about how to resolve the unpopular conflict, which he launched in February with Israel.

But in meetings with his national security advisers and after a series of intelligence briefings, Trump said he was considering holding off on strikes, said the people, who, like others interviewed for this story, spoke on condition of anonymity.

He has also indicated sympathy for allies in the region who have asked him not to return to a full-fledged war.

"I could end it immediately, but at the request of the nations that I am looking to protect, we are doing it a little bit longer way, a bit more civilly," Trump told sports broadcaster Stephen A. Smith on Thursday.

Trump's private comments build on public remarks playing down the likelihood of major warfare resuming.

CALLS WITH SAUDI ARABIA AND TURKEY

In phone calls over the past two weeks, Trump asked for opinions from Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan, who both urged him not to resume attacks on Iran, according to a senior US official and another person familiar with the matter. They said Trump made no commitment either way.

Trump told bin Salman on 31 October that he was planning to attack after the elections, but the crown prince pleaded for him to hold off, arguing that economic sanctions against Iran were working, according to two more people familiar with the discussion.

Saudi Arabia's Foreign Ministry did not respond to a request for comment.

Trump has spoken with Erdogan three times since 28 October, according to Turkey's presidency. An official readout from the 7 November call stressed that tensions between Iran and the US need to end.

MILITARY OPTIONS

At the same time, the US military is ready to escalate if needed, three more people familiar with US planning said.

A third aircraft carrier is moving into the Middle East in the coming days to replace one of the two currently operating in the region, but all three carriers could stay if needed, the people said.

Trump could opt to bomb Iran's underground nuclear facilities, one of the people familiar with Trump's calls with the Saudi and Turkish leaders said. But the US has already struck those facilities, and it is unclear whether further strikes would be successful.

ISRAELI PRESSURE

Israeli officials have continued to lobby the administration to engage in another military campaign, according to a US official.

Trump signalled this week that the US has already achieved what it could from negotiations, but did not say whether he would resume strikes.

Report by Reuters

Iraq sacks nine officials over oil smuggling in pro-Iran group's bastion

Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi dismissed nine officials on Saturday, following an investigation into allegations of oil smuggling in the Jurf al-Sakher area, a stronghold of the Iran-backed Kataeb Hezbollah group.

"In light of the investigation's findings," Zaidi "ordered that all individuals accused of involvement in oil smuggling operations be referred to the judiciary," his military spokesman Sabah al-Numan said, without identifying the suspects. 

The premier "also ordered the dismissal" of nine officials, including security and intelligence officers in Babylon province, an interior ministry commander, and the director of the Oil Pipelines Company at the oil ministry.

Numan did not elaborate on the role of the sacked officials in the alleged smuggling operations.

A committee investigating the allegations entered Jurf al-Sakher on Friday, accompanied by members of Kataeb Hezbollah.

On Wednesday, the state news agency INA reported that "intelligence documents" containing satellite images "showed crude oil and oil-derivatives smuggling operations carried out by an armed faction" in Jurf al-Sakher, accusing the unnamed faction of tapping into a pipeline there.

According to Numan, the investigating committee "confirmed the accuracy" of the information. 

Report by AFP

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] ‘Looking away was never a choice for me’: How Hollywood’s love affair with Israel turned sour
item.description:
‘Looking away was never a choice for me’: How Hollywood’s love affair with Israel turned sour

Submitted by Fleur Hargreaves on Mon, 11/02/2026 - 10:59
A growing number of actors and film workers have been challenging their industry’s ‘deep complicity’ with Israel to end the toxic relationship
US actress Hannah Einbinder wears an 'Artists4Ceasefire' pin as she attends the 83rd annual Golden Globe Awards at the Beverly Hilton hotel in Beverly Hills, California, on 11 January 2026 (Frederic J Brown/AFP)
Off

Once Israel could rely on Hollywood to have its reputation laundered, performing the role of a benign ally which shared the values and interests of the West. 

However, a growing number of actors and prominent figures in film and TV are confronting the industry’s ongoing complicity with Israel's occupation and its actions in Gaza, which a consensus of experts and human rights groups have called a genocide.

More and more artists are using their platforms to speak about the plight of the Palestinians and have contributed to Israel’s cratering approval among western audiences.

In 2025, US-based organisation Film Workers for Palestine (FWP), established by a group of filmmakers the previous year, released a pledge to end complicity with the genocide in Gaza.

It garnered the signatures of more than 5,500 people in the industry, including A-list actors like Josh O’Connor, Olivia Colman, Andrew Garfield, Emma Stone and many more.

Inspired by Filmmakers United Against Apartheid, a group of artists who refused to screen their work in apartheid South Africa, signatories pledged not to screen films, appear at or work alongside Israeli film institutions implicated in genocide and apartheid. 

“People were ready to publicly put their name to a commitment of refusal... to not be complicit in Israel’s genocide,” an FWP spokesperson told Middle East Eye, adding that there is “power in numbers”.

Looking for Gaza in California: How Palestine took over family, Hollywood and campuses
Read More »

A major element of Israel’s “normalisation” is through allowing western films to be shown in Israeli cinemas and festivals, they added, but filmmakers can challenge this by specifying consultation requirements for particular territories in their contracts. 

“I do think there is a sea-change happening,” the spokesperson told MEE, where “people are thinking about their labour and how it is related, how their art is being used".

Many actors wore ceasefire and Palestine pins on the red carpet, using award ceremony speeches and publicity to draw attention to the conflict.

One of the pledge’s signatories, British actor and prominent human rights activist Juliet Stevenson, told MEE that “it was a no-brainer for me to speak up”.

The actor, who is an Amnesty Ambassador, has supported refugee rights throughout her career and last year spoke out in favour of proscribed organisation Palestine Action.

She explained: “I felt I had no option really, looking away was never a choice for me. I don’t know who I would’ve been if I had looked away.”

She added that the potential impact on her career “did not cross my mind”. 

Regarding why more artists and institutions had not spoken out, she said it was “hard to find an answer that isn’t connected to fear, or not wanting to rock the boat”, but as consciousness shifts, more people are emboldened to take a stance, she said.

The recent success of NAZA, an Israeli film featuring soldiers' testimonies of their crimes in Gaza, which received a 25-minute standing ovation at Venice Film Festival, demonstrated for Stevenson that “people in Hollywood who can't seem to operate alone, can seem to stand up with others”.

Corporate consolidation

US film and distribution company Paramount, which was recently acquired by pro-Israel billionaire Larry Ellison, criticised FWP’s pledge as “an effort to boycott Israeli film-makers”.

Since the Ellison family took over the studio, there were reports of Paramount blacklisting talent because of their stance on Palestine, however the company denies this. 

Other sources clarified that, while no itemised list exists, senior management “shares a set of values” and will not work with anyone expressing “hate”.

Paramount under fire for meddling in Gaza coverage after '60 Minutes' producer resigns
Read More »

Mark Ruffalo, star of Marvel’s The Hulk and a vocal pro-Palestine supporter, faced accusations of antisemitism from Ellison after criticising Paramount Skydance's controversial $111bn merger with Warner Bros Discovery. 

In a social media post, Ruffalo highlighted links between Paramount, run by CEO David Ellison, and Oracle, the firm owned by his father Larry, whose surveillance technology maintains Israeli apartheid and occupation. 

Ruffalo shared a video of former Oracle CEO Safra Catz stating that “we have some really profoundly scary technology at Oracle, and we wanted to make sure it was available for the effort”, referring to the Israeli military’s response to the 7 October 2023 attacks.

“Look how [Catz] revels in what we now have come to see as a genocide, which was built on an apartheid system of oppression powered by Oracle,” he commented.

“These ‘really profoundly scary technologies’ will most likely be merged into one of the largest media conglomerates in the world and one day be used on you,” Ruffalo warned, urging opposition to the merger, which he said would be “catastrophic” for the entertainment industry. 

The media giant accused Ruffalo of using “antisemitic tropes” in criticising a deal which would put one family in control of much of American media, including news channels CNN and CBS, and streaming platform HBO.

In response, over 180 prominent Jewish figures signed a letter defending Ruffalo against the “false and dangerous weaponisation of charges of antisemitism”. 

Union failures

Ruffalo is not the only actor to face institutional backlash for supporting Palestine.

In November 2023, Susan Sarandon was dropped by her talent agency after speaking at a pro-Palestine rally, while Melissa Barrera was fired from the Scream franchise for resharing a post accusing Israel of “genocide and ethnic cleansing”.

While the US actors’ union SAG-AFTRA rallied against talkshow host Jimmy Kimmel's suspension by ABC for criticising US President Donald Trump, it remained silent on the repression of actors opposing Israel.

, “The tide has changed,” Amin El Gamal, chair of SAG-AFTRA’s National Middle Eastern and North African Committee, told MEE, referring to the climate ater 2023.

But Hollywood’s “gatekeepers have largely not caught up to public opinion”, remaining unresponsive to union members’ demands to end their “deep complicity” in Israel’s crimes.

He cited the union’s pro-Israel statement issued six days after 7 October, when the death toll in Gaza had already surpassed the number killed in the Hamas-led attack, describing it as “helping justify ongoing genocide”. 

"Go birds, fuck ICE and free Palestine." Hannah Einbinder turned her Emmy win for best supporting actress in a comedy into a platform for activism, wearing a red Artists4Ceasefire pin and joining fellow actors on the red carpet calling for an immediate ceasefire in Gaza. In a follow-up interview, Einbinder said the cause was deeply personal, citing friends working as doctors and teachers in Gaza. She added that as a Jewish person she feels a responsibility to distinguish Judaism from the state of Israel, and voiced support for the Film Workers for Palestine boycott, saying it “does not boycott individuals, it only boycotts institutions that are directly complicit in the genocide.”

— Middle East Eye (@MiddleEastEye) September 15, 2025

Gamal said he repeatedly reached out to the union asking to discuss the statement, but was ignored.

It took almost a year for senior staff to agree to a meeting after an open letter was published in The Hollywood Reporter, only to reject his committee’s proposal for a ceasefire statement. 

Although SAG-AFTRA, which also represents broadcasters, condemned Trump and Russia for targeting journalists, it failed to comment on Israel’s systematic targeting of Palestinian journalists.

On the Warner Bros merger, the union released a weak statement, calling for “enforceable safeguards” before the deal proceeds, despite its implications for the labour interests that it is supposed to represent.

BDS success

Meanwhile, Norway’s actors union, Norsk Skuespillerforbund (NSF), recommended its members refuse to work with complicit Israeli institutions in line with Boycott, Divestment and Sanction (BDS) guidelines.

It also joined other artists’ unions in an appeal urging Norwegian authorities to review their cooperation with Israel and protect Palestinian culture from erasure.

The Netherlands’ International Documentary Film Festival, the world’s largest documentary film festival, also recently signed the Dutch and Belgian cultural boycott against Israel.

Why Britain's liberal Zionists must watch NAZA
Read More »

Ireland’s Cork Film Festival updated its policy to reject funding from governments “found by the International Court of Justice to violate international humanitarian law” or involved in measures “relating to genocide, war crimes, or crimes against humanity”. 

FWP launched a campaign targeting Germany’s Berlinale film festival over its crackdown on filmmakers and workers using their platforms to draw attention to Palestine.

Often these institutions claim to be apolitical, yet after Russia’s invasion, Berlinale made Ukrainian flag pins, and funded a group of Ukrainian film-makers: a blatant double standard. 

Berlinale receives government funding and is broadcast across Germany, where obsessive crackdowns on pro-Palestinian expression have led to artists being cancelled and deplatformed.

When Israeli-Palestinian film No Other Land won the Documentary Film Award at the Berlinale in February 2024, German politicians accused Israeli journalist Yuval Abraham of antisemitism for criticising his country’s apartheid in his acceptance speech.

No Other Land was also awarded last year’s Oscar for best documentary feature, indicating Academy voters were keen to signal a position on the conflict they were otherwise reluctant to express.

Yet when the Palestinian director Hamdan Ballal was violently attacked by Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank shortly after winning the Oscar, the Academy faced criticism for its lack of response.

'A small number of people have disproportionate amounts of power… and a lot of them are still very aligned with Israel’s interests'

-  Amin El Gamal, chair of SAG-AFTRA Middle East committee

Another FWP campaign targeted Mubi, which accepted $100m in funding from Sequoia Capital, a venture firm deeply invested in Israeli military technology.

Although FWP did not call for a boycott, its campaign prompted a drop in Mubi’s subscriber base and staff revolts, leading the arthouse streaming platform to concede to some of the group’s demands, albeit in diluted form. 

“On the one hand, it’s very hopeful… that we have the hearts of the masses in the US,” El Gamal stated, "but at the same time, increasingly, a small number of people have disproportionate amounts of power… and a lot of them are still very aligned with Israel’s interests.” 

He explained that celebrities hold “large cultural capital and actual capital” which they can lend to amplifying Palestinian voices and solidifying Israel’s status as a “toxic rogue state”.

Israel is “so used to getting their way and evading any kind of accountability, they don’t understand what it means to confront this palpable change of attitude”, resorting to silencing critics and vilifying boycotts, which are non-violent, he continued.

But when it comes to “a few billionaires against the masses”, he said, through cultural boycotts and collective action, “people power will always win”.

Book sells out and tour tickets in demand after comedian reveals she contributed to Walliams investigation

When the comedian Lucy Beaumont revealed she had intervened to support a junior TV worker concerned about David Walliams’ behaviour, she feared it would brand her as a troublemaker and ensure she would never work in television again.

The immediate response to her actions, however, has been more heartening. Her book Drinking Custard: The Diary of a Confused Mum sold out online soon after she talked about her fears for her career. There was also a flurry of online posts from fans buying tickets to her current tour, with many posting messages of praise and support.

Support for anyone affected by sexual abuse issues is available in the UK from Rape Crisis on 0808 500 2222 in England and Wales, 0808 801 0302 in Scotland, or 0800 0246 991 in Northern Ireland. The National Association for People Abused in Childhood (Napac) offers support for adult survivors on 0808 801 0331. Samaritans can be contacted on freephone 116 123. Other international helplines are available for people affected by sexual abuse and childhood abuse, and people in crisis.

item.title: [World news | The Guardian] Iran targets Bahrain airbase as strikes resume in Gulf - Middle East crisis live
item.description:
Bahrain lies directly across Persian Gulf from Iran and is home to US Navy Fifth Fleet

Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said they had launched six drones targeting a US air defence radar at the Al-Rifaa helicopter base on Sunday morning, reported Iranian media.

They said they had attacked the air base in retaliation for “hostile US actions”. The base is about a 30-minute drive south of Manama.
